# `SEG_H1 ↔ SEG_V1` — one conversation, both segmenters, both tables pinned

The gold re-annotation ran under the **eval harness** segmenter
(`eval/curator/sid.py`, `SEGMENTER_HARNESS_VERSION = 1`). The product ships a
different implementation — the Rust `SEG_V1`
(`src-tauri/src/memory/adaptive/curator/segment.rs`, `SEGMENTER_VERSION = 1`).
Sentence IDs in `eval/curator/gold_sid/` are therefore comparable to a Rust
run's IDs only *where the two agree*, and until this directory existed **no
fixture pinned them together**. `MANIFEST-V1.md` carries that as a standing
caveat; the acceptance walk carries it as the last of its standing flags.

This is the fixture that closes it.

## The files

| file | what it is | who pins it |
|---|---|---|
| `transcript.jsonl` | host JSONL — what `PARSER_V1` reads | — |
| `unit.txt` | the flat `USER:`/`ASSISTANT:` framing `build_units.py` writes, over the **same sanitized bytes** | — |
| `expected_seg_v1.json` | the Rust `SentenceTable`, serialized | `curator_seg_parity.rs::seg_v1_table_is_pinned` |
| `expected_render.txt` | `RENDER_V1` over that table | `curator_seg_parity.rs::seg_v1_render_is_pinned` |
| `expected_seg_h1.json` | `sid.enumerate_unit(unit.txt)`, plus a `materialized` map of `sid → text` | **Wave 4b-E's Python test** |

`expected_seg_h1.json` was generated by running the committed
`eval/curator/sid.py` over `unit.txt` and is committed unedited. The Python
side owes it one test:

```python
# eval/curator/test_seg_parity.py  (Wave 4b-E)
import json, pathlib, sid
FIX = pathlib.Path(__file__).parents[2] / "src-tauri/tests/fixtures/curator/seg_parity"
def test_seg_h1_table_is_pinned():
    text = (FIX / "unit.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    want = json.loads((FIX / "expected_seg_h1.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    got = sid.enumerate_unit(text)
    assert got["segmenter_harness_version"] == want["segmenter_harness_version"]
    assert got["sentences"] == want["sentences"]
    assert {str(s["sid"]): text[s["start"]:s["end"]] for s in got["sentences"]} \
        == want["materialized"]
```

The Rust side additionally asserts (`both_segmenters_see_the_same_sanitized_bytes`)
that every `ParsedRecord.sanitized` string appears verbatim inside `unit.txt`,
so the two halves cannot drift apart into two different documents.

## What the fixture exercises

Abbreviations (`i.e.`, `Dr.`), decimals (`1.5 s`, `2.0 s`, `p95`), a clock time
(`03:30`), a fenced code block, a three-line ISO-stamped log run, CJK
(Japanese, two sentences, no spaces), and one credential that `REDACT_V1`
replaces with `[REDACTED:api_token]`.

## The divergences

Pinned as assertions in
`curator_seg_parity.rs::the_documented_divergences_are_exactly_these`. A change
that makes a row stop being true — **in either direction** — fails that test.
These are the mapping rule, not a bug list.

| # | what | `SEG_V1` (Rust, product) | `SEG_H1` (Python, harness) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **redaction** | the redaction range is a *hard* boundary: the placeholder is its own sentence with `cite_ok=false`, and the prose either side stays citable → `S4`/`S5`/`S6` | no redactor; consumes text `build_units.py` already redacted and marks the whole containing **sentence** uncitable → one `sid` |
| 2 | **sentence count** | 12 | 10 — the entire gap is divergence 1 |
| 3 | **CJK** | UAX#29 *does* break at `。`, then the short-segment merge immediately re-joins the halves (`word_count` is whitespace-based, Japanese has no spaces) → **1** sentence | boundary regex is `[.!?]+["')\]]*[ \t]+`, which never matches `。` → **1** sentence |
| 4 | **short-segment repair** | merges a `< MIN_SENTENCE_WORDS` (3) segment *forward* into its successor; a trailing one has no successor and stays alone (`"for staging."`) | a closed abbreviation list; merges nothing |
| 5 | **offset basis** | **byte** offsets into **one record's** `sanitized` string; they restart at 0 per record | **character** offsets into the **whole** `unit.txt`, globally monotonic, counting the `USER: `/`ASSISTANT: ` markers |
| 6 | **roles** | a two-valued enum (`user`/`assistant`) derived from host structure; tool records are skipped visibly | a free string over four values (`user`/`assistant`/`tool`/`system`) plus a `role_inferred` flag for a unit that opens without a marker |
| 7 | **cap** | `MAX_SENTENCES_PER_UNIT = 150`, overflow split at record boundaries by `split_units` | `DEFAULT_MAX_SENTENCES = 0` — uncapped, so a benchmark unit is never shortened relative to the anchor baseline |
| 8 | **rendering** | `RENDER_V1`: one `S{n} [role]: ` entry per sentence, opaque-block continuation lines indented two spaces | none — `run_bench.py` builds its prompt from the unit text directly |
| 9 | **opaque blocks** | fence rule + `≥3` log-shaped lines | **identical**, deliberately kept in step (see the comment on `LOG_SHAPES`) |
| 10 | **`sentence_index`** | 0-based within its record | **identical** — the one coordinate the two tables genuinely share |

Rows 3 and 4 are worth reading twice. The two implementations **agree** on the
CJK line and on `"Understood. The patch is below."`, but for unrelated reasons.
That agreement is a coincidence of two different rules, not a contract:
raising `MIN_SENTENCE_WORDS`, or making `word_count` script-aware — which is
the *correct* fix, since the merge exists to repair UAX#29's over-splitting on
English abbreviations and has no business firing on CJK — breaks the agreement
on the Rust side alone and silently re-points every Japanese sentence ID.

## Consequences for the benchmark

* A `gold_sid` offset must **never** be compared to a receipt span. Different
  units (bytes vs characters) over different documents (record-relative vs
  unit-global).
* A `gold_sid` **sentence ID** is comparable to a product run's ID only for a
  unit with no redaction, no CJK, and no `MIN_SENTENCE_WORDS` boundary case —
  i.e. only when rows 1, 3 and 4 all happen not to fire. One credential in a
  unit shifts every ID after it by two.
* The nine `TOOL_RESULT` gold items are unreachable under `PARSER_V1`
  (row 6) and ungradable for `source_role` besides — the output schema offers
  two roles, so there is no right answer to grade a tool-sourced claim
  against. Exclude them by name, never silently.

## Regenerating

Deliberately, or not at all. `expected_seg_v1.json` is what `SpanIdentity` is
built from: a silent change re-points every stored citation. A real SEG_V1 rule
change needs a `SEGMENTER_VERSION` bump, an `IDENTITY_VERSION` bump with it,
and migration/replay fixtures — rewriting this golden is the last step of that,
not a shortcut around it. The same discipline applies to
`SEGMENTER_HARNESS_VERSION` on the Python side.
